title: AI design patterns
author: Jing Hu
description: Reusable design patterns for AI products, written down from the shopping, video and accessibility work of product designer Jing Hu.

themes.name: AI across modes
themes.lede: Answers that cross text, images, video and buttons, and the design work of letting information flow between them.
themes.intro: A shopping video holds an enormous amount of decision-relevant information, but the cost of getting it out has always been too high. Multimodal AI changes that: it can read a frame, find the seconds that matter, and write an answer that mixes words, pictures and clips. The question that sits under every pattern in this theme is the one I get asked most at work: when an answer crosses text, images, video clips and action buttons, how should that information flow?

themes.name: AI in shopping
themes.lede: Helping a shopper get from a question to a confident purchase, with AI doing the finding and the shopper keeping the judgment.
themes.intro: What shoppers really want from a video is not to play it but to ask it. Some will happily watch a thirty-minute review as a kind of window shopping; others want one answer and treat the video as a knowledge base; most sit in between. The patterns here are about serving all three without taking the decision away from the person making it.

themes.name: AI for accessibility
themes.lede: Designing for as many senses as possible, and finding that the structure AI adds to media is the same structure accessibility has always asked for.
themes.intro: I like designing for as many senses as possible: operating a video with the keyboard alone, making sense of one with no sound, or making sense of one with no picture. Once a video has structure, can be read and can be asked, it becomes friendlier to screen readers, silent viewing, keyboard navigation, low-bandwidth connections, older users and people with cognitive differences. In the work this site is drawn from, accessibility was not a patch after launch. It was the foundation.

stages.name: Ask
stages.text: The person has a question, or a thing they want to find.

stages.name: Answer
stages.text: The AI returns something: a clip, a marker, a segment, a generated answer.

stages.name: Check
stages.text: The person looks at the evidence and decides whether to believe it.

stages.name: Decide
stages.text: The person acts: buys, moves on, or corrects the AI.

article-d.title: From watching to asking: how AI is reshaping how we consume shopping videos
article-d.note: A feature about my video shopping work; the patterns on this site are my own English write-up of the same work.

updates.text: Site opened with the first eight patterns, all from the video shopping work covered in the multimodal theme.
